The lecturer reminds you that dreams are evidence; the class reminds you they're also very funny.|Your turn with the dream diary. The class leans in; your entries have a following.} {Last night you dreamed about a goat in a crown.|Last night you dreamed your teeth were made of keys.|{season == "winter": Last night you dreamed of snow falling upward.|Last night you dreamed of an exam in a language made of birds.}} Read the real one aloud {You read about the goat. The class interprets it as ambition, appetite and possibly a farm. You go pink, and learn more than they do.|You read the dream of key-teeth. The lecturer finds three meanings in it; the class finds four, one of them rude.|You read it straight. The interpretations are thoughtful and humiliating, in equal parts.} Invent something impressive {You describe a dream of a silver hare on a staircase. The lecturer is deeply moved. You must remember to have it someday.|You invent a prophetic dream so convincing that half the class writes it down. The lecturer gives it full marks and a worried look.|Your invented dream gets a round of applause. You almost wish it were true.} {You get the silver hare's symbolism backwards. The lecturer, who keeps a book of real dream symbols, notices, and says so, gently, in front of everyone.|You overdo it. Nobody dreams in footnotes. The class is delighted to say so.|Halfway through, you forget what the hare was doing. The class finishes your dream for you, badly.}
